EIA-861M Tennessee monthly sales fit in vanderbilt-data-science/cascading-heat (temp_energy_sale_model.ipynb): 75 degF threshold, +2.38%/degF overall (residential 3.81, commercial 1.66, industrial 0.68). Literature supports load rising with temperature: Bartos et al. (2016) 'peak per-capita summertime loads may rise by 4.2%–15%'.
Threshold of the same EIA fit.
Utilisation of a substation transformer at the design temperature. No Nashville loading data available.
Design air temperature at which K = K_design. Placeholder near the local summer extreme; replace with the utility planning value.
Rated top-oil rise over ambient. Values typical of 65 degC-rise mineral-oil transformers (rated hot spot 110 degC at 30 degC ambient = 30 + dTheta_TO_R + dTheta_H_R); confirm against nameplate data.
Rated hot-spot rise over top oil; see C-P2.dTOR.
Ratio of load losses at rated load to no-load losses (typical range); unit-specific in practice.
Oil exponent for ONAN (self-cooled) cooling.
Winding exponent for ONAN cooling.
Top-oil time constant (order of hours for ONAN units); unit-specific.

Hot-spot temperature with 50% hourly failure probability. Placeholder anchored on the C57.91 caution against hot spots above ~140 degC (gas-bubble risk; to be confirmed against the standard text); not a measured fragility. Fragility-curve form after Shinozuka et al. (2000).
Dispersion of the hot-spot fragility.

Capacity C = (1 + alpha) L_design (Motter & Lai 2002: overload cascades when loads redistribute). Values are the overload thresholds 1.15 / 1.35 / 2.45 used in the cascading-heat Monte Carlo (120,000 runs).

'failure of nodes in one network may lead to failure of dependent nodes in other networks. This may happen recursively' (Buldyrev et al. 2010). Physical dependency in the sense of Rinaldi et al. (2001).
Time a thermally failed substation stays out. Replace with NES restoration statistics when available.
Hospitals must maintain emergency/standby power (CMS Emergency Preparedness Rule 81 FR 63860). Probability that backup fails on demand is a placeholder.
Long-term care facilities must plan alternate energy sources (81 FR 63860); coverage of cooling loads varies. Placeholder.
Dialysis depends on power and water; Kelman et al. (2015) document disrupted dialysis care and excess deaths after Hurricane Sandy. No backup assumed (placeholder for facility-level data).
'During the blackout, mortality increased for … nonaccidental (ie, disease-related) deaths (25% [12%-41%])' (Anderson & Bell 2012). Reported for context; not applied to a mortality baseline in v0.

'the concurrence of a multiday blackout event with heat wave conditions to more than double the estimated rate of heat-related mortality' (Stone et al. 2023). Lower bound used as a context factor only.
Facilities lose water only when every production source is down and storage is exhausted. Hydraulics are not modelled in v0 (a WNTR-type model, Klise et al. 2017, is the intended upgrade).
Treatment/pumping plants usually have standby generation; probability of failure on demand is a placeholder.
Hours that towers / covered reservoirs keep supply after all production stops. Placeholder.

Median at the high-temperature grade of a PG 64 binder (AASHTO M 320 grading). Underwood et al. (2017): 'stationary assumptions have resulted in incorrect material selection for 35% of 799 observed locations'. LST is used as a proxy for pavement surface temperature (assumption).
Dispersion of the pavement fragility.
Share of signals without working battery backup. Placeholder.
A dark signal degrades control on the segments it governs (cyber/physical dependency in Rinaldi et al. 2001). Capacity loss is not quantified in v0.
Recorded for completeness; no heat fragility for bridges in v0.
Recorded for completeness; access is not routed in v0.
Population in a zone shares the zone's power state (areal allocation of ZCTA counts).
Air temperature above which an outage hour counts as a compound heat exposure. Placeholder; temperature–mortality curves are city-specific (Gasparrini et al. 2015).

Intake temperature at which once-through cooled plants (EIA-860 cooling type ON: Cumberland TN 2,470 MW; Gallatin TN 1,556 MW) start to derate. Concept after van Vliet et al. (2012); the permit limits of these plants are not available. The fitted stream-temperature model gives summer maxima of 26–27 degC for 2014–2025.
Temperature range from the start of derating to full curtailment.
Discharge at USGS 03431500 below which intake is curtailed. Observed summer minima 2014–2025: 4,420 (2023) – 8,550 cfs.
Share of plant capacity lost while discharge is below Q_min.

Share of TVA operable summer capacity (38,472 MW in EIA-860 2022) available after forced and planned outages. Constrained in calibration: TVA did not shed load in the summers 2015–2025 (EIA-930 summer peaks 28,764–32,126 MW).
Net import capability available to TVA at peak.
Capacity of a signalised link when its signal is dark, treated as an all-way stop (HCM). Placeholder.
BPR coefficient.
BPR exponent.
Per-lane capacity of interstates, freeways and expressways (HPMS f_system 1–2).
Per-lane capacity of signalised arterials (f_system 3–4).
Per-lane capacity of collectors and local streets (f_system 5–7).
